obligation: CPNI breach notice to law enforcement (current rule)
trigger: Reasonable determination that a person, without or exceeding authorization, intentionally gained access to, used, or disclosed CPNI (64.2011(e)). In this scenario: call detail exported from the VoIP portal or home phone signaling captured at the router
deadline: As soon as practicable and no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination
notify: USSS and FBI electronically through the FCC central reporting facility (link at fcc.gov/eb/cpni)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - provider of interconnected VoIP service (64.2003(o)) for the 58 home phone lines; no size exemption

obligation: CPNI breach: hold on customer and public notice
trigger: Law enforcement notice filed
deadline: No customer or public disclosure until 7 full business days after the USSS and FBI notice, notwithstanding contrary state law. Earlier notice only if the company flags an extraordinarily urgent need in its notice and consults the investigating agency; the agency may direct a delay of up to 30 days, extendable
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI breach notice to customers (current rule)
trigger: Law enforcement notice process complete
deadline: After the hold ends (or as the agency directs). The current rule sets no further outer deadline, so plan to the Florida clock below
notify: Each home phone customer whose CPNI was breached
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI breach record
trigger: Any CPNI breach discovered
deadline: Record kept at least 2 years: dates of discovery and notices, description of the CPNI, circumstances
notify: Internal (incident log, CPNI breach section; POL-01 10.4)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: CPNI and covered data breach notice (2023 amendments; NOT yet effective)
citation: 47 CFR 64.2011 as amended by FCC 23-111 (89 FR 9968); upheld in Ohio Telecom Ass'n v. FCC (6th Cir. 2025-08-13)
trigger: Would cover inadvertent as well as intentional access, and customer PII as well as CPNI
deadline: Would require FCC, USSS, and FBI notice within 7 business days; customer notice without unreasonable delay and within 30 days after reasonable determination; breaches under 500 customers with no reasonably likely harm reported in an annual summary instead
applies_at_this_tier: No - amendments remain delayed indefinitely; no FCC effective-date notice found in the Federal Register through 2026-10-05. Recheck at every incident

obligation: CALEA compromise or unlawful surveillance report
trigger: Any compromise of a lawful interception or of access to call-identifying information, or any act of unlawful electronic surveillance on company premises. An attacker capturing home phone signaling at the edge router may be unlawful surveillance on the company's premises; counsel decides
deadline: Within a reasonable time upon discovery
notify: Affected law enforcement agencies (FBI field office; any agency with an active order)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - CALEA carrier as a facilities-based broadband and interconnected VoIP provider (70 FR 59664)

obligation: 911 special facility (county 911 center) outage notice
trigger: Outage that potentially affects a 911 special facility as defined in 4.5(e). Every trigger that could apply needs 900,000 user minutes, which 58 lines cannot realistically reach
deadline: As soon as possible and no later than 30 minutes after discovery, by telephone and in writing; first follow-up within 2 hours
notify: Designated outage contact at the county 911 center (confirm yearly, 4.9(h)(1))
applies_at_this_tier: Applies, but the threshold is not expected to be met. If isolating the router cuts home phone service, still call the wholesale provider and post customer notice that 911 by home phone is down

obligation: FCC outage report (interconnected VoIP)
trigger: VoIP outage of at least 30 minutes that potentially affects a 911 or 988 special facility, or 900,000 user minutes with complete loss of service, or special offices and facilities
deadline: Notification within 240 minutes (911 or 988 facility affected) or 24 hours (other triggers); final report within 30 days
applies_at_this_tier: Not expected - 58 lines would need more than 10 days of total outage to reach 900,000 user minutes. Recheck if lines pass 1,000 (POL-01 10.6)

obligation: DIRS daily reporting
trigger: FCC activates DIRS for the county (for example, a hurricane during the incident)
deadline: Daily infrastructure status reports from activation until deactivation
applies_at_this_tier: Unclear for a reseller of VoIP over its own broadband network; counsel to confirm by 2027-05-31 (P03 G-045)

obligation: Florida breach notice to individuals
trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents. Personal information includes a user name or email address with a password or security question and answer, and name with SSN, government ID, or financial account with access code. Call detail alone may not qualify; counsel decides
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred. Notice under the primary or functional federal regulator's rules is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs; counsel decides whether FCC CPNI notice qualifies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if Florida-defined personal information is involved (for example, portal credentials taken from the billing platform or laptop)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - about 310 accounts; recheck the count of affected individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - about 310 accounts

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice (inbound from vendors)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the company (billing platform, VoIP provider, AI assistant vendor) has a breach
deadline: Vendor must notify the company within 10 days of determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - track in vendor terms (POAM-009)

obligation: State data breach notification (other states)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents of other states (about 10% of residential accounts belong to seasonal residents)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransom or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Statute: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - no final rule published as of 2026-10-05. Voluntary report to CISA and the FBI instead

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05
trigger: Material cybersecurity incident at a public registrant
deadline: 4 business days after materiality determination
applies_at_this_tier: No - sole proprietorship with no securities

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Covered equipment or services found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Kaspersky covered article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Kaspersky covered article found while performing a federal contract
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - no federal contracts or subcontracts

obligation: Wholesale VoIP provider notice
trigger: Suspected compromise of the reseller portal account or toll fraud
deadline: Immediately per the provider's fraud line; the agreement sets no deadline
notify: Wholesale VoIP provider fraud and support line
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not regulatory
